reviews.review:
At present, I am writing about the Pre-1.0 release of this game so consider that if reading in the future. But, for what's here, it feels like a real attempt at learning from the two other shooter games already under their belt while also navigating what made Deep Rock Galactic the success it is today. 

DRG is about co-operation, team play and efficient action. Rogue Core bumps that up to overdrive by making a game all about doing these things better than you've ever done them before, or die. The new parts to help make the hoards of core spawn managable, is the addition of the Roguelike bits which make for an experience that's lengthy but enjoyable.

Before, you're abilities are locked in at the loadout menu and the variance comes from what you encounter in the mission. DRG is great but once you land on kit you are comfy with, it's hard not to feel like there's no point jumping to anything else. This works; why change? Rogue Core forces you to get better with a range of kit, though there isn't enough in the game yet to really stretch that out. Rogue Core introduces more weapons, a couple new tools but also kicks out some key kit. 

Like the Grappling Hook, which I can only imagine is for balancing reasons. The Scout can cover so much ground in a short amount of time, it would make the hurried nature of a mission facile. Just zip from A to D, skipping B and C, slap the elevator awake and be done in 5 minutes. That said, the Flare Gun is still here except I'm not sure how helpful it is except for spotting particluar threats on the ceiling. The caves don't always get very big and nothing is hard to spot (especially Expenite, which glows bright green, unlike Nitra and other resources) so it's the only tool that feels like an outright dud at present.

The rest of the new kit is pretty neat. Mainly side arms and rifles, as many standard weapons that hit hard have now been designated a 'Heavy Weapon' that must be found. If you loved your Minigun like a child, you'll now need to find them in the caves and make do with either a accurate charging pistol or a plasma rifle that gives the plasma carbine competition. It's good to see the standard kit from DRG in here too, especially old reliable staples like the Deepcore and Zhukovs though it's fun to realise they're no longer class locked. Mixing and planning around what my character can do is consideration that's worth the time.

Indeed, the new characters and their powers are very cool through require a little muscle memory to use. I have it set that I have to toggle the power equipment and while it is an adjustment, it's quickly become like pulling out drills or the grappling hook to access my class' special powers. I can dash with Slicer to pick up things from awkard places, keep enemies under control with Guardian, have Falconer what my back and so on. For something in early access, all of the characters are pretty well designed to cover some aspect of the upgrade pool or handling the hoards of monsters coming after you in different ways. No one is fully support or aggro (except maybe Retcon) but they're all able to fill any roll required. 

Most of this is down to the upgrades themselves being very potent once you get more than one under your belt. There's still a clear debate over whether to build and get upgrades early or wait until you get a 'Luck' bonus between missions but I feel I would prefer to have even common or uncommon upgrades ASAP to ensure I can even get to where I am going. Some builds can feel like they get broken or fun to play with really easily but that's necessary because the core spawn aren't messing around. 

Honestly, it starts to feel a lot like DRG Themed 'Gunfire Reborn' but DRG builds on that by making you commit to a gun, making building around it much easier, and giving more upgrades more often. Lots of choices often, all for doing the things you do anyway. Every gain, especially big amounts, of Expenite will cost you time that's ticking down to a constant wave and horrid monsters that are looking to drag you away off the map. You need to be efficient and getting busted OP is a good way to beat the tide back. Though. skillful use of what you have been given can pay off too. 

Still, each character leans into particular upgrades best. Spotter can gain 100% Critical Hit chance, so will want anything that procs of that more than anyone else. Falconer specialises in electric damage, Guardian can stun reiably, Slicer can lean phenominally well into melee which is surprisingly effective in this game if you get more than one stack of Vampire. Retcon is the odd one because they're effectively a retooled Chaser from Overwatch. Which is fun but has a higher skill floor than everyone else. 

In fact, this game is just plain harder. I have many hours in DRG, maining Scout, and it's apparent that you will need every ounce and gram of skill from your time mining to handle reclaiming work. Compared to the glyphids, core spawn are faster, meaner and can hop around ensuring that they'll not fall for all the same tricks. Certainly not convincing a core spawn you're a friend and recruiting it into the team as a 'Steve'. They're here for blood. 

Partly it's because you have only one gun and a traversal tool, that's it. But also because these things have to stand up to a roided up Reclaimer with a tricked out pistol that crits for thousands of damage. Even then, the core spawn feel like a threat at all times in ways that the glyphids could only manage at the very highest difficulties. 

Even so, to make things easier, missions are less explore-y. Most expects a straight-shot to the finish, but there's still plenty to bounce around finding. All of it will help somehow, it just depends on how long you want to spend. That time limit feels strict. Especially with 4 players. 

But the tone and feel of the game seems to reflect the heavier stakes. DRG is kinda jovial, a bit of a piss around and a doss at the bar before you load up and ship out. It's not funny, persay, but it's not taking itself particularly seriously either. You can paint yourself bright blue and dress up as Papa Smurf; DRG is supposed to be fun.

Rogue Core isn't entirely devoid of humour or that similar energy, but it's definately muted and wants to present itself as a more focused, almost-hardcore game incomparison. The Reclaimers are billed as an elite group with better tech than the mining crew we've gotten used to. They don't have Mission Control, they have a slightly egotistic AI called Omega running things with an eye on efficiency. The Ramrod is grayer and, currently, not dressed quite as comforting as the Spacerig. Even the Hall of Heroes and the promotion system gets it's own unique animation, lending pomp and circumstance to the act of making your character icon a little fancier. It all serves to push the idea that you are going to have to give more than you have done before to succeed here. 

This reverence makes Rogue Core feel a little more serious, as this is the next part of this world and the fictional company, we're getting to see. It characterises the Reclaimers as being more elite very effectively compared to the more lackadaisical Mining crew of DRG. I even like the detail that while the mining crew is perfectly fine-ish to go to work blind drunk, the Reclaimers have to earn their drinks by working out and staying in shape, turning their calories burnt into a currency. Its a small change but speaks volumes.

At present, I am enjoying this game. I am looking forward to what else they add. I think more ways to move around and alter terrain would be excellent to see before any new guns or dwarves. Though very exciting to think that we might get new (or old) classes in the game. 

Also, a fantastic feminist move of not gender locking anything. Ladybeards for all! As it should be!

rogue core is fun, but there are many gameplay issues i have right now. i have faith that GSG can iron these out in the future but it seems shaky for now.

tl;dr immense amounts of artificial difficulty, resupplies are gimped from DRG, upgrade system is clunky and can be annoying with a team

near constant swarms with enemies that all do tons of damage, and are also either immensely bullet spongey, move faster than you, have ranged attacks that delete 1/3 of your health or all at once. weapons having little to no ammo for how much damage they do. weakpoints not feeling rewarding in terms of damage, especially for the relative difficulty hitting them compared to DRG. all of these feel bad by themselves yet also cascade upon each other and become exponentially more annoying when you factor in the horrible team based upgrade system.

you need to huddle around and tell campfire stories to get upgrades. people are either running around across the level at a constant 80m+ away from you or hounding you to get closer for one (1) upgrade while not moving to close the gap quicker themselves. this is made even more of a problem with the constant voicelines when entering the zone, the zone being so miniscule that you could only fit a bough wasp in between all 4 players, and that one guy who is desperate for mid swarm upgrades to get health back because there isnt any red sugar.

resupplies in drg were a perfected system. 80 of a common material for 4 slots that restore +50% ammo, equipment, and health that you could call whenever you wanted. a godsend for duo and solo players, and perfectly balanced for when there are trios and quads. you could always reliably get at least 3 resupplies in every mission, alongside lootbugs which would always have enough you an additional 2 per mission. you even got more nitra in boss fight type mission where youre expected to use large amounts of ammo in bursts like Escort Duty, Industrial Sabotage, and Elimination.

meanwhile in rogue core, theyre spawned randomly and spread, only usually 2 or 3 per level, and have a single slot per player in mission. absolutely kills ammo economy for people that play with a partial group or solo because you just get straight up less ammo. less players means less total ammo & less total damage, but it is also compounded with less players meaning less slots on the resupplies. this is without even considering we dont have 

Deep Rock's total ammo formula would be ( x players ) + ( 4 * 0.5 * resupply pods called down )
Rogue Core's total ammo formula would be ( x players ) + ( x players * 0.5 * pods spawned )

and speaking of supplies, there seems to be so little health for some reason? maybe friendly fire and other chip damage has just became more noticeable since they removed regenerating shields with an armor that progressively degrades after taking damage.
its just not it .Deep Rock Galactic is way better .

2 cent from a DRG vet here.

1. Game is stressful & rushing with timer thing, dev should've made it OPTIONAL for people do not have much time to play but still want to enjoy 'upgraded' version of DRG.

2. Again, not much time to play but still have to work out in-game to earn point FOR BUYING BEERS?! This is an addition to UNNECESSARY BS. Just make it as a CASUAL and OPTIONAL SIDE GAME like in DRG where you can kick barrel or play knock-off flappy bird to kill some times while waiting. GRINDING MISSION IS ALREADY STRESSFUL, DONT FORCE US TO GRIND MINI GAME TO BUY BEERS.

3. PLEASE CUT THE TIME WASTING & BS SPAWN WITH NO GUNS & GEARS. Putting a few lines for the dwarves to speak does not make it legit.

4. Weapons crate is close to nothing useful (mostly from weak weapons of Gunner & Engineer in DRG without mods). Adding a few more new weapons does not mean get rid of majority of the old weapons in DRG.

If you engage with the game not as a derivative of DRG but as its own spinoff it works pretty well. For new players it's pretty difficult, more like difficulty 4 in DRG, but going deeper into the progression might fix this. I would like more variety of end-bosses in the first few missions, as it gets boring otherwise. I don't mind the timer, but I think it does add a lot more stress to the experience. I think in general the game is a lot more interactive between players and can be played less as a multiple single players in one lobby game. In drg there's fewer occasions where you need to negotiate and/or plan together. I think it's easier to play and chat about something else while playing in drg than in rogue core. I have not played with online players that I don't know, but I can imagine it's more difficult to play rogue core with them than drg. The fact that every mission ends with a boss fight, and a difficult one at that, means that generally missions are pretty stressful in general. It needs more explanation in the negotiation screens about what all the different types of damage are, what crit damage is and what the current crit parameters are, how much dps you're making etc. I'm sure they can add this over time, but currently it seems like you're really making choices in the dark. Based on the choices and what appears to be a lot of randomness, the weapons do feel pretty good, and are well designed in themselves.
Good game, I have a lot of fun

It's frustrating right now cause runs can be extremely hit or miss depending how lucky you are on the upgrades. The amount of enemies feels overwhelming sometimes given how fast they move compared to regular DRG and they hit much harder, which combined with the armor system feels way too punishing. The game being more punishing is fine but I feel like there's too many punishments stacked here. Low ammo, downgraded armor, faster and harder hitting enemies, time limit and so on.
There's good parts too, like more cooperative play, classes and abilities, most of the guns feeling nice, as well as the decisions you have to make, but a lot of times these are overshadowed by the bigger flaws of the game. The base is solid and can be enjoyable but it has issues that need to be addressed to make it less frustrating.

As a middle level DRG dwarf and Green beard RC dwarf, here's my personal opinion on DRG Rogue Core but I could be just me being crap for being a green beard. 
1.The Reclaimers and general difficultly: The difficulty on this game is significantly harder than reg DRG but the challenge and much faster pace does make it very fun and I have been playing with my little brother for already over 20 hours and brought the game the moment it came out. Personally I think all of them if you don't count the Bio boosters are all perfectly balanced and none of them feel stupidly strong compared to the others! But I think their designs need to look more distinct from each other similarly to the Miners in DRG. But so far besides Slicer and Retcon with Retcon being my favorite, it's impossible for me to clear even a three stage level with them. Spotter's really weak without a team and I think Falconer's long range revive needs reworking for single player because it's basically useless. My Brother says he likes Guardian the most mainly because it's easy staying alive as one.

2.Weapons: At first I thought all weapons are equal but I soon learned some are more equal than others, the Devastator Pistol is my favorite weapon and I would love to see it in DRG and the PGL finally became what I wanted it to be in DRG, but for every Devastator, Shock Striker, PGL, Lead storm and Thunderhead, there's five Warthogs, MM-4 Chargers, Bolt-Tec "Decker" SMGs, Hammercasters, and to make a long story short, crap guns that make you want to rip open the equipment locker with a Drillerdozer. The grenades also didn't translate very well over from DRG, mainly because in DRG you tossed them when you wanted to burst something big like a Pretorian down or clear up a huge swarm. But in this game, the grenades fail at both of them because even the damage ones don't do enough damage to knock out big threats and the swarm busters can't clear up space either.
Gameplay is not good for a roguelike game for now.

As someone who started out loving roguelike/lites because of DRG: Survivor, I love the hell out of this game.
Deep Rock Galactic is one of my all-time favorite games, and with 1500+ hours in the original game, this game has a bit of a learning curve that you'll have to adapt to, compared to what you might be used to in the original game. Things are much faster paced, and you don't exactly have a lot of time to dawdle or dilly-dally, so time is of the essence. 
One of the first things you may notice as you complete the tutorial is that whenever you fall from a relatively high point, instead of continuing to run forward, your dwarf will stagger for a brief moment, before moving at normal speed again. This can be circumvented with a couple of methods, such as platforms or certain upgrades.
If you get greedy and let the threat timer reach maximum, you're gonna have a rough time, unless you're just [i] that [/i] guy, or have an insanely overpowered loadout.
The biggest thing you have to watch out for if you do end up reaching maximum threat level, are the [spoiler] Reaperworms [/spoiler].
Spoiler: [spoiler] If you let one grab you, it will gradually drain your hp and draw you back into its burrow. If you are in a group and it successfully reaps you, you're gone until the next level. You'll keep any weapons and expenite you may have had on you, but your team will have to release you from an alien cocoon thing and revive you upon exiting the elevator on the next level. If you're playing solo and Cooper does not save you, or, your whole team including yourself get grabbed by Reaperworms, that's it. Your run is dead. [/spoiler]
Speaking as someone very familiar with Deep Rock Galactic, you'll find that the difficulty curve ramps up quite quickly in Rogue Core compared to the original game. Your depth level (1-4) essentially corresponds to what your Hazard level would be. Complexity plays a big role in how difficult a facility (mission) can be, a lot more so in Rogue Core than I consider to be the case in DRG. 
Each facility is essentially just its own Deep Dive, your initial weapons and cave layout remain the same upon multiple runs of the same facility, though you usually will not be able to play the same facility more than once, unless if you speedrun it maybe. As opposed to having 3 set levels per Deep Dive, each facility in Rogue Core will have 4-6 levels, and at the very last level, when you reach the very end of the cave system you will be faced with 1 of 3 bosses.

Some of this is likely subject to change, considering the game is in early access at the time of writing.
As of right now, many changes are coming to the game, along with difficulty options for the threat timer. 
I do believe this game has a lot of places and spots it needs to improve in, but currently as it is, it's still a very fun game, I can definitely see myself switching between the two games occasionally, and wholeheartedly recommend this game if you like Deep Rock Galactic.

reviews.review:
I was gifted this, and have enjoyed my time with it with a few caveats.

This IS mechanically similar to DRG. This is NOT however DRG + Roguelike elements.

I'd better explain this as an efficiency-focused looter-esque shooter. The core gameplay loop revolves around hunting around an unmapped cave with chosen, albeit limited weaponry for upgrades, fighting, and repeating. 

Stuff is rough at present, missing or otherwise incomplete, but what's here is quite fun, although the new player orientation is still quite lacking. I do look forward to it being more clearly explained and having to do less questioning of mechanics.

UPDATE: I see potential for improvement. DRG has certainly lost its touch but I hope to see fixes. 

- This [Team Upgrade-Pick System], where each players picks one at a time, ITS DUMB AND FRUSTRATING AS HELL!!! Who's the bright dev that thought up this feature? Get rid of it or it will kill this game. 

- How about some added progression for players from their time in the original DRG? 

- And must female dwarves be ugly as sin? I'm not saying we need bodacious babes, but I don't particularly enjoy playing butass ugly characters either. Face change cosmetics are sorely needed.

- DRGRC's current gameplay makes teams less cohesive but rather something that you have to put up with

I'm giving a thumbs down because there are some pretty fundamental issues with the game.
The following are my top complaints:

1. Ammo economy is atrocious. In single player it works just fine, but once I queued in a duo, it was so over. Also some weapons like the devastator pistol have absurdly low ammo. The damage isn't good enough to justify its low ammo capacity.

2. Not enough healing. If you have to fight a boss and there's no red sugar, it'll end your run, even on lower difficulties.

3. If the boss orbs spawn on higher ground than the terrain behind them, trying to grab the orbs and go uphill or up a cliff can also just end the run. It's brutal.

4. Class exclusivity is non-optional. If you pick one class, nobody else in the party can pick that class. This should be optional. The fact that it's not is just not fun. I want to be able to go duo slicer if I want to. That would be so fun.

5. Certain upgrades are just never picked. There's an upgrade that gives guaranteed crit chance on the first round in your magazine. If the game was a slower pace, that might have interesting niche builds. But rogue core demands that you keep running and keep firing. Reloading just for that crit round is just too risky.

6. I understand the game is meant to be more difficult than DRG, but it feels like the run 100% depends on upgrade and weapon RNG, and not on your ability to make use of whatever you get. It feels bad when I lose because it feels like I lost due to bad game mechanics and not because of my lack of skill. The word I have in my mind every time is "brutal".

7. There's no sell/recycle mechanic. I think that some ability to recycle or trade upgrades would be good. Other roguelikes allow you to make up for bad RNG by selling/recycling items and then being able to buy replacement items later. 

I love the franchise, and I'll keep playing the game. I bought this game on the day it released and the supporter pack. I believe in it. I'll give it a thumbs up once everything's addressed. RNS

I did not play DRG all that much, it wasn't really my type of game.
I should also mention that the above literally doesn't matter, because this isn't DRG, it's just apart of the same world.
As of the time of this review, I played one game with a single friend, and a second one solo. Both were wins.

Reading through other reviews, I don't understand why people say this game is too hard. Even lore-wise it makes sense that this game is harder than DRG. You play as a Reclaimer. And these guys are supposed to be the bad-a**es that that clear out as many enemies as they can, while also getting the lost facilities up and running. These are the same areas in DRG that are grayed out, that are apparently overrun with baddies, and so you can't mine there.

The whole point of this game is to run through the deep facilities and do the main objectives (repairing the facilities or decimating a strong baddie, side objectives too if you've got the time. Go at a decent pace, don't be too slow, and you'll have no issue getting done in time. It's meant for some decently serious co-op play too, since the rogue-lite mechanics are shared between everyone.

If you don't have a group of people you can talk to in a vc to play with, I DO NOT recommend this game for you. Playing with randoms on public is not the way to go. You can't communicate well enough or fast enough to pick out what the upgrades you'd like. Not to mention, even if there was an in-game vc (there might be I didn't check) you can't expect everyone to use it.

Overall, if you want mildly difficult, relatively fast-paced gameplay, this is it.

Plays like base DRG in terms of gameplay, just with randomized weapons/equipment/grenades. Needs more time to cook and become better. 
I've played most of the game as a duo with my friend.

When upgrading everyone needs to be near the mule to trigger them, and it's a shared upgrade pool instead of individualized, so everyone chooses an upgrade round robin style and the first upgrade taken is no longer available for other players. 

A lot of the weapons feel bad baseline and need some good RNG to get the upgrade to make them good. For example SMGs need a recoil reduction to make them viable. If you luck into an elemental weapon (40% dmg as fire/poison/electricity) then you are able to go a weapon build and have it be actually viable considering how limited ammo feels against the hordes of enemies roguelikes have you face. 

The meta progression upgrade don't feel impactful enough considering you can only use 8 of them at one time. Some of the meta perks feel useless, like HP regen threshold. If you have no armor and regen to that amount, you are still able to be downed in like 2 hits, maybe 3 if you play enough to get the 4th tier of the perk.
The basic enemies in base DRG can be funneled fairly easily, but in rogue core they can jump so even when you manage to funnel them they can just jump and attack and chip away at your hp/armor. In base DRG you have a shield that regenerates, it's not a very big shield but it's a means to retain health for playing well and cushions you against some bad enemy spawns. Having some means to resist chip damage  would help with balancing.

There is a very strict timer. I get having a timer in that it forces you to move, but here you literally have to keep pushing as fast as you can otherwise you'll hit the timer and face more foes than your limited ammo can handle. By being forced to move so fast you can easily miss side objectives and miss crucial power upgrades that you need to make it through a run. There is also a reaper worm after the timer hits which is pretty much a 1shot if you get grabbed  and pulled to the next level (if aren't saved by your teammates).  The reaper worm is less of an issue considering how deadly the normal enemies are and how you are getting swarmed and killed by the time it appears. 

The Jump between depth 2 to depth 3 is crazy high in terms of difficulty. Considering how badly RNG can screw you over, I don't feel I will make the choice to try and go further in terms of depths.  Comparatively to base DRG, where it does get fairly difficult going from 2 to 3 to 4 then to 5, but you can build out your kit to go into those missions, rather than rogue core where you are dealt a hand and have to try and make it work at the same level of difficulty. 

Each class does feel different, but some abilities could use some work. For example the slasher has a short range dodge as an ability, but I feel that it doesn't go nearly far enough to be useful in getting out of danger or using it for getting to places too high or wide to normally reach without using your equipment ammo. 

While this is a start for a DRG FPS roguelike, it seems that they wanted to change some core functions that make co-op roguelikes work. Like shared upgrade pool, needing people to literally gather around to get said upgrades. In other co-op roguelikes some builds take longer to come online and if one player gets completely screwed via RNG,  a different player can get good enough RNG to carry or at least survive until things improve. 

They did a much better job for a roguelike in DRG: Survivor. It was well balanced and most of the RNG in the game comes from what weapons you choose during your run in addition to what weapons are available. You are able to reroll as well so if you get really poor RNG you can actually reroll it and hope for a better option. 

If I do want to continue playing this I'll probably play on Depth 2 and wait for things to improve. It'll probably take a few months to a year or so. Currently not worth the asking price. If they keep up with the roadmap and actually take a lot of the feedback people are giving them, then it'll likely be better and worth the asking price.

Well it's in early access and boy does it show, balance is kind of a mess right now.  A lot of weapons are just awful and can't really deal with the hordes in any meaningful way so if your first level doesn't give you a viable weapon then you might as well just die and restart.  Running multiplayer is sort of mixed, you get more people to fight the hordes but the RNG aspect gets annoying.  When solo you get 4 options with 1 being a constant + hp or w/e but each extra player just adds 1 more option for rng meaning that adding players doesn't really help mitigate bad RNG with upgrades/weapons/etc.  In other co-op rogue-likes you can at least rely on one player getting a high roll to carry, you can't do that here so if your collective rng is crap then your run won't go well for the most part.  It also hurts to have 1 epic and 3 green choices and only one person grabs it, I play with friends so we try not to grief but when all the options aside from the legendary/epic/rare are bad it just feels like crap, assuming you even get above green rarity (I had a run where we got 0 rare/epic/legendary for the first 2 levels and it was awful).

Ammo economy is just bad, you can take all the ammo perks you like and it still won't solve the problem once you get to depth 3+, there's just too many and you can't kill them with the ammo you have unless you high rolled a very good weapon and upgrades for said weapon.  The timer is fine on depth 1-2 but once you get to depth 3 there's not enough time to find the side objectives or mine enough expenite to keep your power high enough to kill the hordes.  It might get better with a full party of 4 but when playing solo or duo it's a nightmare to get objectives besides getting to the elevator complete.  Difficulty balancing is also kinda ass right now, since even the basic enemies get a huge distance closing leap and instantly attack you upon landing, there's nowhere safe to be unless you're in a tunnel and force them through a chokepoint.  Unfortunately if you want to get enough power to win in depth 3+ then you have to fight them in bad spots to try and make your way to something that can give you a decent power spike (if rng favors you anyways).

Game runs fine, haven't had any performance issues so that's a good part at least.

Most zones are incredibly dark even with your basic flares and unless you're picking the flare gun it's hard to find all the enemies before they get to you (mostly because of that damn leap).  Compared to the time I spent in the regular DRG, the enemies in that game didn't have huge gap closing capabilities and there were downtimes between foes to get objectives done.  For this game the timer (again) causes huge issues, you need to kill enemies fast in order to make spare time to get objectives done but if your rng is bad and you don't get good weapons or good perks then you fight enemies for 3 minutes instead of 1-2 and now the next wave is coming in 30-60 seconds.

Maybe this game will get better in a year or 2 but I don't have any hopes for it in the near future.  It also doesn't really look or feel all that different from the base DRG so my friends who played that and didn't like it won't give this one any attention so I'll have to wait for patches to make this better.  I don't trust random pugs to not grief me with upgrade picks either so there's no point in matchmaking imo.

I wanted to give it some time before giving this a review.  It's definitely a different experience to Deep Rock Galactic, and I'm glad they spun it off instead of making it a mission type or whatever the original plan was.

It's much harder than DRG.  The timer gives it a very frantic feel, which I like.  All the familiar weapons, grenades, and equipment is here, along with some new ones.  It feels great to make combinations you wouldn't be able to do in DRG.

The roguelike mechanics work well, and I LOVE sharing upgrades with my teammates.  It makes it feel much more cooperative than your typical multiplayer roguelike.

A great early access release, and I'm looking forward to watching it progress to a 1.0 release.

I understand the negative reviews. A lot of people were expecting DRG2 and got something different. Roguelite games aren't for everyone, they aren't for me but I'm still having fun in this game.

People complain about the time, which I get, you could take your time in DRG, but not here. The timer is not nearly as bad as people make it out to be, you just need to play with some urgency.

People complaining about female dwarves need to get a life, it's 2026, women exist, get over it.

I was concerned when I heard a lot of feedback was ignored during the alpha playtests but they are now acting on early access feedback and will be making some important changes soon. They should have listened sooner, but I'm glad they are listening now.

If you like DRG and you like roguelite games, then you'll enjoy Rogue Core. If you enjoy roguelite games, you'll probably enjoy Rogue Core. If you just like DRG, maybe hold off for a few updates, but you still might like the game.

If you don't like DRG or roguelite games, then why are you even here?

I hereby petition to rename the entire Rogue-Lite genre to "Lottobotomy".

Half of the time, I'm offered upgrades that actually synergize, and I get to have a nice little power trip.  The other half of the time, absolutely nothing works together and I'm left with the same feeling as picking glass shards out of my heel.  Which experience I get is a complete dice-roll.

I'm left with the question of who exactly the Rogue-Lite genre appeals to, other than people who are scared of their own thoughts and just need to play the game [i]now[/i] with no setup.

A few hours worth of games later, and the fun/glass-in-heels ratio has slipped closer to 1:4.  This game is an absolute slog to try and learn what it wants from me, and I am not finding much enjoyment in any of it.  I fully regret the purchase and time I've spent on it.

A foundation for a fantastic Deep Rock Galactic roguelite game is here, but it needs more time in the oven before I can fully recommend this for the same price as the original. For now, I would recommend it only to those who like the DRG formula and roguelites, and trust the developers to continue adding more features and level types to the game...which I do. 

Their upcoming patch responding to the most critical pain points shows they are listening well to feedback. They are even adding in auto-sprint, which they didn't even cave to adding in the original game, for years. We will be able to upgrade without having everyone sitting at Ellis, which is huge for the game's pacing. 

Things are looking even better the closer we get to release. In Early access? It needs more time, but I'm leaning favorably because I got my money's worth already - with more content on the way.

I really enjoyed this one. There's enough content for 40-60 hours of play, and it feels like a good spinoff to DRG. I experienced a handful of bugs, but I had fun with the time I've already spent and I'm looking forward t o seeing the finished product.
The tempo of the game is so much faster that DRG. And Im loving it.
